activity.role: Commander of German forces in North Africa
activity.notes: Erwin Rommel arrived in North Africa with the German intervention in February 1941 and commanded successive German and German-Italian formations there until March 1943. The organizational command changed from the Deutsches Afrikakorps to larger Panzergruppe/Panzerarmee and Heeresgruppe formations, so ATLAS uses the historically accurate umbrella role 'Commander of German forces in North Africa' rather than pretending he held one unchanged unit command throughout 1941-1943. The Activity is attached to the existing higher-order Germany polity; 'Nazi Germany' is a regime-period label, not a separate territorial polity in the ATLAS model.

sources.title: Der Afrikafeldzug — Bundesarchiv
sources.citation_text: The German Federal Archives records the arrival of the German Afrika Korps under General Erwin Rommel in February 1941 and traces the subsequent North African command formations through 1943.

sources.title: Verbände und Truppen der deutschen Wehrmacht und Waffen-SS 1939-1945, Band 14 — Bundesarchiv
sources.citation_text: The Bundesarchiv-hosted Tessin reference lists Rommel as commander of Heeresgruppe Afrika from 23 February 1943 until Hans-Jürgen von Arnim took over on 10 March 1943, confirming the endpoint of Rommel's North African command period.
